column6: Rigid-body L splits into orbital (CM) plus spin parts; CM motion helps but fixed-axis L=Iω stands alone.
Reducing a two-body central-force problem to one body uses reduced mass.
Real collisions (crashes, restitution) are mostly inelastic; B analyzes them directly.
Zero net torque -> L conserved follows from τ = dL/dt; rigid-body L already hard.
Concrete energy-transfer intuition helps the formal KE+PE bookkeeping.
B is spring/ODE/eigenvector coupling; string tension is not what it draws on.
U_eff = U(r) + L²/2mr² requires U(r) from a conservative central force.
Inelastic collisions are a standard example of irreversible KE loss to heat.
FBDs for equilibrium cases use the net-force-zero condition of the first law.
Friction problems are typically set on inclines; concrete incline intuition helps.
Precession Ω = τ/L draws on torque and L, not the rolling constraint.
B derives T² = 4π²a³/GM from gravitation, though the empirical laws stand alone.
Conceptual projectile intuition (independent x/y) supports formal 2D kinematics. Note: B oddly lists reduced-mass-two-body as a soft prereq.
Lagrangian intro works in configuration space; phase space belongs with Hamiltonian mechanics.
B connects G m₁m₂/r² to F = mg; mass vs weight distinction underlies that link.
Effective potential gives the standard analysis of bound elliptical orbits.
Real two-body orbits (binaries) use reduced mass; not needed for fixed-center orbits.
Power P = F·v does not draw on mechanical advantage of simple machines.
Reduction uses the CM frame and relative coordinate; frame-change skill helps.
Rolling analysis uses ω, α and τ = Iα of rotation, alongside the existing hard prereqs.
τ = Iα about a pivot often needs I via parallel-axis theorem.
Concrete wheel-and-axle gives torque intuition for formal rotational dynamics.
½Iω² uses a given I; perpendicular-axis theorem is a niche I-computation tool.
Dominant direction is rotational KE -> rolling energy analysis, not the reverse; mutual otherwise.
Conceptual inertia precursor; formal newtons-first-law is already a hard prereq.
Lever balance is the concrete prototype of torque equilibrium.
Concrete balance/stability intuition supports formal equilibrium conditions.
B's core examples are elastic collisions viewed in the CM frame.
Inclines show work = force x distance trade-off concretely.
Mechanical advantage trading force for distance motivates the work concept.
Screws are a narrow simple machine; inclined-planes and mechanical-advantage already cover the intuition.
Work as energy transfer is the conceptual basis of W_net = ΔKE.
